problem: The term 'log[Cl⁻]²' is ambiguous: a student can read it as (log[Cl⁻])² instead of the log of the squared concentration.
fix: Write E = E° − (0.0592/2) log([Cl⁻]²), and add that this is the same as E = E° − 0.0592 log[Cl⁻], so raising [Cl⁻] lowers the potential.

problem: The range is given as 'about pH 1 to 12' with no warning about the errors at the ends of that range, so a student may trust readings near pH 12.
fix: Add: near and above pH 9–10 the glass gives the alkaline error, and below about pH 1 the acid error, so readings at the extremes are only approximate unless a special glass is used.

problem: The cell is written as glass | test solution || KCl (sat) | Hg₂Cl₂, Hg, which leaves out the inner Ag/AgCl reference and the 0.1 M HCl inside the glass bulb, so the notation does not match the parts described just above it.
fix: Write the full cell: Ag | AgCl | 0.1 M HCl | glass membrane | test solution || KCl (sat) | Hg₂Cl₂ | Hg.
